Name: help
Details: Without a command, shows an overview of available slash commands.
With a command name, shows detailed usage and examples.

Name: about
Details: Opens the About SeraphIRC panel with version and build information.

Name: alias
Parameters: name: shortcut name, with or without a leading slash
command: slash command to run when the alias is used
Summary: Create or update a command alias
Details: Creates or updates a shortcut for another command. Built-in SeraphIRC commands and built-in command aliases cannot be overwritten.
Run /alias without arguments to open the Aliases settings page.

Name: unalias
Details: Removes a user-defined command alias.

Name: connect
Summary: Connect the active network or request a server link
Details: Without arguments, starts a connection for the active network if it is disconnected.
With arguments on a connected network, sends IRC CONNECT to request a server link.
Note: IRC CONNECT usually requires IRC operator privileges.

Name: disconnect
Details: Immediately closes the active network socket without sending a graceful IRC QUIT.

Name: reconnect
Details: Reconnects the active network using the same behavior as the Reconnect menu action.

Name: znc
Parameters: module: optional ZNC module target such as controlpanel, sasl, nickserv, or perform
Details: Sends a command to ZNC's *status service.
Use /znc <module> <command> to send to a ZNC virtual module such as controlpanel, sasl, nickserv, or perform.
/znc is available only for ZNC-backed networks.

Name: cycle
Parameters: #channel: optional channel to part and rejoin
Details: Parts and immediately rejoins a channel on the active network. Without a channel, uses the current channel buffer.

Name: quit
Details: Gracefully quits the active network by sending IRC QUIT. Use /disconnect to immediately drop the socket without sending QUIT.

Name: ignore
Parameters: nick or mask: a nickname, or a nick!user@host mask with * and ? wildcards
Summary: Ignore a nick or mask on the current network
Details: Ignores messages, notices, CTCP and invites from a sender on the current network, and hides their joins, parts, quits and nick changes. Uses the same ignore list as the user context menu.
A bare nick means that nick only, so it stops applying the moment they change it. A mask keeps holding: * matches any run of characters and ? matches one.

Name: unignore
Parameters: nick or mask: the entry to remove, spelled as it was added
Summary: Stop ignoring a nick or mask
Details: Removes an entry from the current network ignore list using the same state as the user context menu. Remove it the way it was added: /unignore Alice does not clear a *!*@spam.example that happens to cover her.

Name: exit
Details: Closes the SeraphIRC desktop application.

Name: close
Details: Closes the current channel or query buffer and switches to a fallback buffer when available.

Name: clear
Summary: Clear the current visible buffer without deleting logs
Details: Clears the visible transcript for the current buffer without deleting saved logs.

Name: clearall
Parameters: -a: clear all buffers across all servers
-s: clear all buffers on the active server
Summary: Clear visible buffers without deleting logs
Details: Clears visible transcripts without deleting saved logs.
Use -a to clear all visible buffers across all servers.
Use -s to clear all visible buffers on the active server.

Name: join
Details: Sends JOIN to the IRC server and opens the channel buffer locally.

Name: part
Details: Without arguments, parts the current channel. With a channel, parts that channel and uses any remaining text as the part reason.

Name: partall
Summary: Leave all joined channels on the active network
Details: Leave all currently joined channels on the active network. This does not disconnect from the network and does not affect channels on other networks.

Name: query
Parameters: nick: nickname to open as a private query
Details: Opens a private query buffer with a nick. Use /msg if you want to send a message immediately.

Name: msg
Summary: Send a private or target message
Details: Sends PRIVMSG to the target and echoes it into the matching local query or channel buffer.

Name: notice
Details: Sends NOTICE to a nick or channel and echoes the outbound notice locally.

Name: me
Details: Sends a CTCP ACTION to the current channel or query buffer.

Name: format
Summary: Send one message with text formatting applied
Details: Applies markdown (_italic_, __bold__, ~~strike~~, `code`, ||spoiler||) and token ($b, $i, $s, $u, $m, $c) formatting to this message regardless of the auto_format setting.

Name: plain
Summary: Send one message with text formatting disabled
Details: Sends the message exactly as typed, overriding the auto_format setting for this message.

Name: format-me
Parameters: action: action text with formatting syntax
Summary: Send an action message with formatting applied

Name: format-msg
Summary: Send a targeted message with formatting applied

Name: format-notice
Parameters: message: notice text with formatting syntax
Summary: Send a NOTICE with formatting applied

Name: plain-me
Summary: Send an action message with formatting disabled

Name: plain-msg
Summary: Send a targeted message with formatting disabled

Name: plain-notice
Parameters: message: notice text to send verbatim
Summary: Send a NOTICE with formatting disabled

Name: ctcp
Parameters: command: CTCP command such as VERSION or PING
Details: Sends a CTCP request as a PRIVMSG with CTCP framing.

Name: notify
Parameters: nick: optional nick to add or remove
comment: optional note saved with the entry
Details: Without arguments, opens the notify list. With a nick, toggles that nick in the active network's notify list.

Name: server
Details: Opens the active network's server/status buffer.

Name: switch
Parameters: buffer: channel, query, or server buffer name
Details: Switches the current buffer for the active network.

Name: current
Details: Displays the current buffer for the active network.

Name: buffers
Details: Lists buffers for the active network, including buffer type, message count, and unread count.

Name: show
Parameters: count: optional number of recent messages to show, default 20
Details: Prints recent messages from the current buffer as local server-style output.

Name: state
Details: Lists buffers and their message counts for the active network.

Name: dcc
Parameters: path: file to send (a picker opens when omitted)
Summary: Send and receive files directly with another user
Details: DCC transfers files straight between the two computers, with no server in between.

Because of that it needs a DIRECT connection: it is unavailable on networks that go through a bouncer (soju or ZNC), where the address the transfer would use belongs to the bouncer rather than to either person.
Incoming offers also appear as cards in the buffer and in the transfers panel, so these commands are a keyboard shortcut rather than the only route.
/dcc get with no nick accepts the only waiting offer, and resumes automatically when part of the file is already downloaded.
SeraphIRC does not support DCC chat.

Name: seraphchat
Parameters: nick: the person to invite (in a query it defaults to that person)
Summary: Start an encrypted direct chat with another user
Details: Seraph Chat is a direct, end-to-end encrypted conversation between two computers: nothing crosses the IRC server, nothing is logged, and closing the window discards the transcript on both machines.
Unlike DCC it works from behind a bouncer, because the connection is set up through the Seraph rendezvous rather than through addresses in IRC messages.
Accepting or sending an invitation reveals your IP address to the rendezvous immediately and to the other person once both sides agree, which is why the first use asks for confirmation.
The command never reaches the server. Invitations also start from a nickname's right-click menu, so this is a keyboard shortcut rather than the only route.
Nothing to set up: Seraph Chat is available on every network, including through a bouncer.

Name: seraphtransfer
Parameters: nick: the person to send to (in a query it defaults to that person)
Summary: Send a file directly with Seraph Transfer
Details: Opens a file picker and offers the chosen file over Seraph Transfer: a direct, end-to-end encrypted transfer that verifies the file and, unlike DCC, works from behind a bouncer.
The same action as "Send File (Seraph)" in a nickname's right-click menu, so this is a keyboard shortcut rather than the only route.
Sending an offer reveals your IP address to the rendezvous immediately and to the other person once they accept.
The command never reaches the server, and it never falls back to DCC by itself: if the peer cannot answer a Seraph offer, DCC is suggested rather than silently used.
Nothing to set up: Seraph Transfer is available on every network, including through a bouncer. Settings > File Uploads & DCC tunes where files land and how large an offer may be.

Name: giphy
Parameters: search terms: what to look for (omit to browse what is trending)
Summary: Open the GIF picker, optionally with a search already run
Details: Opens the GIF picker above the composer. With search terms it runs that search. With none it shows what is trending.

The command never sends anything by itself. Attach puts the GIF's link in the composer and leaves it there, so you can add a comment, and so the message goes out through the same checks as anything else you type.
Off until you turn it on. The integration needs a free Giphy API key of your own: Settings > Integrations > Giphy Integration.
When enabled, your search terms and IP address are sent to Giphy. GIFs you post are links to Giphy's servers, so anyone whose client displays them also connects to Giphy.

Name: whois
Details: Requests WHOIS information from the IRC server.

Name: whowas
Summary: Shows information about a user who has quit
Details: Sends WHOWAS to the IRC server for the requested nickname.

Name: nick
Details: Requests a nickname change. This is also allowed while registration is blocked if the socket is open.

Name: away
Details: Marks you away with an optional message.

Name: back
Details: Marks you as back by clearing away status.

Name: topic
Details: Without text, shows the current channel topic. With text, sends a topic change for the current channel.

Name: names
Details: Requests NAMES for a channel. Without a channel, uses the current channel and avoids network-wide NAMES output.

Name: list
Details: Requests the network channel list and opens SeraphIRC's searchable channel list UI.

Name: mode
Details: Sends a raw MODE command to the IRC server.
The target can be a #channel or a nickname. Use your own nick to view or change your user modes: /mode <yournick> shows your current modes, and /mode <yournick> +i sets one (e.g. +i for invisible).

Name: knock
Parameters: #channel: the invite-only channel to request entry to
reason: optional message shown to the channel operators
Summary: Request an invite to an invite-only channel
Details: Sends a KNOCK to an invite-only (+i) channel, asking its operators to invite you. Availability and exact behavior depend on the server.

Name: accept
Parameters: +nick: allow this nick to message you
-nick: remove this nick from the list
Details: On networks with the caller-ID user mode (+g), the ACCEPT list controls who may send you private messages and notices. Use +nick to allow someone, -nick to remove them, and * to list the current entries.

Name: motd
Summary: Fetch the server Message of the Day
Details: Requests the server Message of the Day. MOTD numerics display in the existing server/status output.

Name: who
Details: Sends WHO to the IRC server.

Name: ban
Parameters: #channel: optional channel when not issued from a channel buffer
Summary: Ban a nick or mask from a channel
Details: Sends MODE +b. Without an explicit channel, uses the current channel buffer. Nicknames are converted to nick!*@* masks.

Name: unban
Parameters: #channel: optional channel when not issued from a channel buffer
Summary: Remove a ban from a channel
Details: Sends MODE -b. Without an explicit channel, uses the current channel buffer. Nicknames are converted to nick!*@* masks.

Name: kickban
Parameters: #channel: optional channel when not issued from a channel buffer
nick: nickname to ban and kick
Summary: Ban and kick a user from a channel
Details: Sets a ban mask and then kicks the nick. Without an explicit channel, uses the current channel buffer.

Name: op
Parameters: nick: nickname to give operator status
Details: Sends MODE +o for a nick in the current channel.

Name: deop
Parameters: nick: nickname to remove operator status from
Details: Sends MODE -o for a nick in the current channel.

Name: voice
Details: Sends MODE +v for a nick in the current channel.

Name: devoice
Parameters: nick: nickname to remove voice from
Details: Sends MODE -v for a nick in the current channel.

Name: invite
Parameters: #channel: channel target, defaulting to the channel you are currently viewing
Summary: Invite a nick to a channel
Details: Sends INVITE to the IRC server. If you omit the channel while viewing a channel, the current channel is used.

Name: kick
Parameters: #channel: optional channel when not issued from a channel buffer
Summary: Kick a user from a channel
Details: Sends KICK to the IRC server. Without an explicit channel, uses the current channel buffer.

Name: raw
Parameters: IRC line: raw command text to send
Details: Sends the provided IRC line exactly as typed after /raw. /quote is an alias.

Name: users
Details: Sends IRC USERS to the active network. Server support and output vary by IRC network.

Name: lusers
Details: Sends IRC LUSERS to request local and global user/server counts for the active network.

Name: time
Details: Sends IRC TIME to request the server time. With a server argument, requests time from that server.

Name: admin
Details: Sends IRC ADMIN to request server administrator information.

Name: info
Details: Sends IRC INFO to request server information, if supported by the network.

Name: ison
Parameters: nick: one or more nicknames to check
Details: Sends IRC ISON to check whether one or more nicknames are currently online.

Name: userhost
Parameters: nick: one or more nicknames to inspect
Details: Sends IRC USERHOST to request user and host information for one or more nicknames.

Name: oper
Details: Authenticates as an IRC operator. The password is sent to the server but is redacted from local output and command history.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges.

Name: kill
Details: Forcibly disconnects a user from the server.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges.

Name: kline
Details: Sets a server-level host/IP ban. If the second token looks like a duration, SeraphIRC sends it before the mask.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: unkline
Details: Removes a server-level K-line.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: gline
Summary: Set a network-wide ban, if supported
Details: Sets a network-wide ban on networks that support GLINE.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: zline
Summary: Set an IP-level ban, if supported
Details: Sets an IP-level ban on networks that support ZLINE.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: shun
Summary: Silently block commands from a user
Details: Silently blocks commands from a user on networks that support SHUN.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: squit
Details: Disconnects a server from the network.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges.

Name: rehash
Parameters: config: optional config name or target
Details: Reloads server configuration without a full restart.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: restart
Details: Restarts the IRC server. A reason is required.
Note: Destructive. Requires IRC operator privileges.

Name: die
Details: Shuts down the IRC server. A reason is required.
Note: Highly destructive. Requires IRC operator privileges.

Name: stats
Details: Queries server statistics.
Note: Some flags may require IRC operator privileges.

Name: links
Details: Lists linked servers.
Note: Some networks restrict this command.

Name: map
Details: Shows the network topology map on servers that support MAP.
Note: Syntax and availability may vary by network.

Name: trace
Summary: Trace a user or server route
Details: Traces the route to a user or server.
Note: May require IRC operator privileges.

Name: globops
Details: Sends a message to all online IRC operators.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges.

Name: wallops
Summary: Broadcast to users with wallops enabled
Details: Broadcasts to users with wallops enabled.
Note: Requires server permission on many networks.

Name: locops
Details: Sends a message to local IRC operators on the current server.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges.

Name: cloak
Details: Manages or requests hostname cloaking where supported.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: uncloak
Details: Removes hostname cloaking where supported.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: sethost
Details: Sets a user's displayed host where supported.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: chghost
Details: Changes a user's displayed host where supported.
Note: Requires IRC operator privileges. Syntax may vary by network.

Name: silence
Details: Manages server-side silence entries. Syntax varies by network, so use /raw for network-specific syntax.

Name: nickserv
Details: Sends a private message to the configured NickServ target for the active network.

Name: chanserv
Details: Sends a private message to the configured ChanServ target for the active network.

Name: memoserv
Details: Sends a private message to the configured MemoServ target for the active network.

Name: helpserv
Details: Sends a private message to the configured HelpServ target for the active network.

Name: hostserv
Details: Sends a private message to the configured HostServ target for the active network.

Name: botserv
Details: Sends a private message to the configured BotServ target for the active network.

Name: operserv
Details: Sends a private message to the configured OperServ target for the active network.
